chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: A Greek cabaret night out and arrest by the Sudanese police
summary: Chittison took Butler to a Greek cabaret full of German girls, took a woman's pocketbook home, and at dawn a seven-foot Sudanese policeman fetched both men.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now in the meantime, I'm hanging out with the Arabs, not Arabs, but Egyptians, then I became (inaudible) Egyptians. I was learning to speak, Mohammed passions; that was big and big and Chitte son was still running around, so one night Chitte son said come with me, I know a place where all the pretty women in the world are, and I said, well, Chitte son you didn't come down here with no women, I got mine over there. He said, man, will you please come with me. I'm going to a Greek carabet.

Now all the girls in there were German girls, very pretty girls and we sit in the booth awhile, drinking and they was -- Antonette was a lady who comes in the place, and she dressed, beautiful, you buy champagne or whatever and she
get a certain percentage off each bottle.

Antinurse, it's a French word, so Chitteson had been going down there and it looked pretty good down there, and we got into the booth and Chitteson was -- there was another tall one, redheaded girl, she liked me. She liked me very much. All the girls were from Germany and I could speak German, so we was making it pretty good, but Chitteson seemed to have a problem, so Chitteson decided that he would take this girl's pocketbook and go home with it and the girl would follow him up to his room.

I said, Chitteson, what are you doing. He said, oh, this woman likes me and she'll be up soon. At 5:00 that morning I was asleep inbed, at that time the Sudanese were the police, Sudanese was a man about seven feet tall, and they had them swords, those long swords. The sword was as tall as Chitteson, and if you did anything, he wouldn't hesitate.
